Subject: Data residency / deletion for PHI — quick Qs

Vivek — thanks for the demo earlier. Two quick compliance questions from our security/privacy lead before we proceed to an internal pilot: 

1) What are realistic retention limits you can guarantee for PHI-containing input and generated outputs? We need to show timelines for deletion when we commit to our regulators — 30/90/365 day options?

2) Does Redwood offer built-in redaction at ingest or do customers need to run post-processing? Can you describe approaches (pre-tokenization redaction vs token-level filtering) and caveats about model behavior after redaction?

We’re evaluating hosted vs dedicated/private deployment for this pilot — priorities are certifiable deletion and key custody. Happy to take a brief follow-up call if easier.

Phil

Phil — great to hear from you, and glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front, details below and attached a one-pager (redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf):

• Retention windows: hosted API supports configurable ephemeral retention policies we can set per-customer — common presets are 30 / 90 / 365 days. For Dedicated and Private, customers control retention via configuration and we support contractual SLAs for deletion and proof of deletion.

• Redaction: we offer multiple options — ingest-time redaction hooks (regex and token-aware scrubbing), streaming redactors before model input, and post-generation filters. In hosted mode we provide managed redaction templates; in Private mode you can run local processors and manage keys.

Notes/caveats: token-level redaction is more robust for model prompts (prevents tokens from entering KV cache), but it's harder to prove what was never persisted at storage layer unless you run Private/Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. Backups and logs are governed separately — we can include retention constraints in contract and provide deletion certificates for primary data and backups within an agreed window.

If useful I can loop in Laura (Security Product) and Rishi (Legal) for specifics on deletion SLAs and evidence for audits.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Vivek / Phil / team — quick recommended approach from product/security/legal POV (short version):

1) Deployment recommendation: for patient-level PHI recommend Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane or on-prem) or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. Hosted can work for low-risk pilots but you should not rely on hosted if you require certifiable separation of keys / absolute auditability of deletion across backups.

2) Retention windows we can support: 30 / 90 / 365 day presets for primary inference artifacts. For SLAs we can commit to deletion of primary store within 5 business days of request for Dedicated/Private when contractual terms are accepted; for Hosted we typically commit to 30 days but can negotiate evidence timelines. We will include deletion certificates (signed) covering primary data and snapshot deletion within the agreed contract window.

3) Redaction options & practical notes:
  • Ingest-time (pre-tokenization) redaction: remove data before tokenization via customer-supplied scrubbers (regex, PII library). Pro: simple, provable. Con: may over-redact and degrade prompt context.
  • Token-aware scrubbing (preferred for minimal context loss): apply tokenizer-aware filters that remove tokens and purge KV cache before persistence. Pro: better preservation of context; Con: requires careful testing to ensure scrubber covers edge cases.
  • Post-generation filters: good for removing PHI from outputs but doesn’t prevent model from seeing PHI during inference.

4) Audit & backups: backups, audit logs, and monitoring streams have separate retention and will be handled per contract. For Dedicated/Private we can provide tooling to run deletion proof jobs and produce tamper-evident audit logs.

5) Next steps: If Sage wants contractual deletion SLAs and deletion certificates, we need to scope the pilot: deployment type (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), desired retention preset, KMS arrangement, and whether you need eDiscovery-style export before deletion. I’ve dropped a concise runbook link and an example regex file for redaction.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/security/retention-runbook
Attachments: redaction-pattern-examples.txt

If helpful, I can join a 30-minute call with your security/privacy lead to walk through our technical controls and the deletion proof process.

—Laura Bennett
